articleTitle: Session Management for Collaborative Applications in Interactive Grid
publicationTitle: IEEE International Conference on Computer Systems and Applications, 2006.
abstract: Grid computing extends the application domain to include interaction and collaboration, termed as interactive grid. Interactive grid enables various collaborative applications, in which activities involve geographically distributed and heterogeneous resources, SO work together to achieve a common goal. Thus, software support to facilitate coordination among entities is needed. This paper introduces a session management framework for collaborative applications in interactive grid, and describes the mechanisms of session management in detail. Then, a scalable and flexible software architecture based on OGSA is presented, which can adapt to the dynamism of grid resources. Finally, the performance evaluation is given.

articleTitle: Modeling redundancy: Quantitative and qualitative models
publicationTitle: IEEE International Conference on Computer Systems and Applications, 2006.
abstract: Redundancy is a system property that generally refers to duplication of state information or system function. While redundancy is usually investigated in the context of fault tolerance, one can argue that it is in fact an intrinsic feature of a system that can be analyzed on its own without reference to fault tolerance. Redundancy may arise by design, generally to support fault tolerance, or as a natural byproduct of design, and is usually unexploited. In this paper, we tentatively explore observable forms of redundancy, as well as mathematical models that capture them.
